tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the largest disk to the target, and finally move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a contiguous stack of disks between two pegs and you have a free auxiliary peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 from peg 0 to peg 2 while disks 1 and 2 remain on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, check that the source peg’s top disk is exactly the disk you intend to move, and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every move you generate, verify both source and destination constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg that no longer contains it because it was already moved earlier, leading to a missing‑disk error.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you want to move has smaller disks stacked above it, first relocate those smaller disks to other pegs so the target disk becomes the topmost.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a desired disk is not on top of its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disk 2 is still on top of it, violating the rule that only the topmost disk may be moved.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it ideal for temporarily holding other disks while larger moves are performed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a free spot to hold a disk temporarily, move the smallest disk there first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing the smallest disk 1 onto a peg that later needs to be cleared for a larger disk, but forgetting to move it away, causing a blocked move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target blocking disk before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg’s top disk is smaller than the disk you intend to move, first move that smaller disk elsewhere so the larger disk can be placed safely.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 1, which is smaller, violating the size ordering rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already holds some of the final tower’s larger disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the remaining tower on top of them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal peg is not empty at the start of the solution.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a correctly placed disk 5 off the goal peg, then later being unable to restore the correct order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear auxiliary peg of smaller disks before using it for larger moves
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a peg is needed as the source or auxiliary for moving a larger disk, ensure that any smaller disks on that peg are first moved elsewhere so they do not block the larger move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before using a peg as the temporary holder for a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 from a peg that still has disk 1 on top, resulting in a non‑top move error.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto the goal peg only after all larger disks are already correctly positioned.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final configuration from an arbitrary start.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 2 onto the goal peg before disk 4, which later blocks the placement of disk 4 because a smaller disk is now on top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, output it as the last syntactically correct list in the response, using the exact format [[disk, from, to], ...].
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of the answer, before any trailing text.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing no move list or an incomplete list at the end of the answer, so the verifier sees an empty or malformed sequence.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Phase clearing before moving larger disk to final position
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk to its final peg, first clear any smaller disks from that target peg (if present) and also clear any smaller disks that sit on the source peg, ensuring the move is legal and does not disturb already placed larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to place a disk onto its final location.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto the goal peg while a smaller disk remains on top of the goal peg, causing an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on reasoning and forgets to include the final move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Explicitly add a final line that prints the move list in the required format after all reasoning.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model checks only the source constraints or forgets the size rule when selecting a destination.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before committing a move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on the goal position without checking if it is currently exposed on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving it.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops early before printing the full list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Reserve enough space for the entire move list and verify that the list ends with a closing bracket.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of the current state after several moves and repeats a move that has already been performed.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep an up‑to‑date mental representation of each peg after every move and check that the source peg actually contains the intended disk.
